plan: Reduce QQQI to 20% to lower concentration.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to cut risk.
Exit all semiconductor holdings (SMH, MUU) due to weakness.
Sell leveraged AI/Software positions (METU, PLTU) for capital preservation.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall risk.
Expect lower volatility and a more conservative return profile.
conservative.read: This plan aims for capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% monthly return. It significantly reduces leverage and focuses on less volatile assets, aiming for lower drawdowns.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to manage concentration.
Reduce leveraged ETFs (SOXL to 3%, SPAL to 1%) to lower risk.
Sell weak semiconductor (SMH, MUU) and leveraged AI/SW (METU, PLTU) positions.
Buy defensive sector ETF XLV for diversification.
This plan balances risk reduction with growth potential.
Expect moderate returns and controlled drawdowns.
balanced.read: This balanced approach targets ~2.5% monthly return by reducing leverage and concentration while adding some diversification. It aims for risk-first growth with a moderate cash buffer.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to manage concentration.
Increase leveraged ETFs (SOXL to 6%, SPAL to 6%) for aggressive growth.
Sell weak semiconductor (SMH, MUU) and leveraged AI/SW (METU, PLTU) positions.
Buy defensive sector ETF XLV for diversification.
This plan aggressively pursues growth through leverage and concentration.
Expect higher potential returns but also significantly larger drawdowns.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% monthly return by increasing leverage and concentration in high-conviction areas. It accepts higher risk and potential for larger drawdowns, with a smaller cash buffer.

plan: Increase QQQI to 30% to maximize income generation.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to eliminate risk.
Exit all semiconductor (SMH, MUU) and leveraged AI/SW (METU, PLTU) positions.
Sell growth stock CRWD to reallocate to income.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly income over growth.
Expect lower volatility and consistent distributions, but NAV can still fall.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets ~1% monthly return through distributions. It shifts capital to income-generating assets like QQQI and cuts all speculative and leveraged positions. While prioritizing income, NAV can still decline in market downturns.
